utility.value: La Plata Electric Association (LPEA), if it serves your address
utility.notes: The City's Solar Permit Checklist tells applicants to submit an Interconnection / Net Metering Application to La Plata Electric Association (LPEA). The City's Solar page says LPEA has a number of important resources for installing solar in the Durango area. The City and LPEA pages do not say that LPEA serves every address in Durango, and they give no address lookup. Confirm your electric utility with LPEA member services at (970) 247-5786 before you apply.

generation_supplier.notes: The City and LPEA solar pages do not name a separate generation supplier.

county.notes: The City's Land Use and Development Code describes Durango as the county seat of La Plata County.

permit_authority.value: City of Durango Community Development Department (Building Division)
permit_authority.notes: All solar panel installations in Durango require a City solar permit. Electrical work, including photovoltaic installation, is permitted by the State of Colorado Electrical Board, and all electrical permits and inspections are processed by the State of Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies. The City's building codes apply within the city limits of Durango. The City does not publish a way to check whether an address is inside city limits, so ask the Community Development Department if you are unsure.

permit_url.notes: The City's Solar page links the City solar permit application and the solar permitting and installation process checklist and flowchart. The Solar Permit Checklist says to complete a Photovoltaic Solar Permit Application and submit it to the City of Durango Community Development Department. The City's Applying for a Building Permit page says applicants need an account on the OpenGov online portal. The checklist does not mention OpenGov, so ask the Building Division whether to file the solar application online or in person.

interconnection_url.notes: For LPEA members only. LPEA's process starts with an Interconnection Application, and the member must have an account number before applying. LPEA charges a $150 Interconnection Application Fee on the customer's bill upon engineering approval. LPEA says a PV system may also require approval from the Fire Protection District, County or Municipality. Issuance of a City of Durango Photovoltaic Solar Permit does not guarantee approval by LPEA.

battery_programs.notes: LPEA's website lists a Battery Energy Storage System item under Rebates, but LPEA's solar pages do not give its terms. Ask LPEA whether a battery rebate applies to your project.

value.name: LPEA Interconnection / Net Metering Application (LPEA members)

required_documents.notes: From the City's Solar Permit Checklist, which is undated. The checklist says the City issues residential permits under the 2015 International Residential Code, while the City's Building Codes page says the Building Division has enforced the 2024 I-Codes since 01/01/2026. Ask the Building Division whether the checklist is current before you prepare your application.

value: If the site is in a historic or special district, a Planned Development zone, an owner's association or a landmark site, get an alterations certificate, design review or HOA approval first.
Submit the Photovoltaic Solar Permit Application to the City of Durango Community Development Department.
Before installation, get an electrical permit from the State of Colorado.
Before installation, submit an Interconnection Application to LPEA. LPEA's engineering review takes 2-4 weeks.
Sign the LPEA Interconnection Agreement and return it to renewables@lpea.coop.
Install the system and pass the State electrical inspection. Upload your State electrical approvals to your City permit as you receive them.
Submit a Permission to Operate (PTO) request to LPEA within 10 days of turning on the system.
LPEA performs its final inspection within two weeks of receiving the completed PTO request and issues a Permission to Operate certificate upon approval.
inspection_steps.notes: City inspection requests are scheduled through the OpenGov system, and 48-hour notice is required for all inspections. The City's checklist and inspection page do not list a separate City inspection for a solar PV system. The State electrical permit, the City solar permit and LPEA's Permission to Operate are separate approvals.

timeline_days.notes: The City does not publish a review time for a solar permit. LPEA says its engineering review of an interconnection application takes 2-4 weeks, which is separate from the City permit.

value.program_or_pathway: City of Durango Photovoltaic Solar Permit, plus a State electrical permit
other_conditions: The Solar Permit Checklist sends residential projects to Over-the-counter Photovoltaic Solar Permit Review.
Rooftop systems must meet the height restrictions and setback requirements for the zoning district in the Land Use and Development Code, and the manufacturer's installation specifications.
Ground-mounted systems must meet the setback requirements for detached accessory buildings if the highest point on the panel is more than 8 ft above grade.
For a commercial solar installation, the City says that depending on the visibility of the solar installation, solar reviews require either Building staff review or a public meeting.
Homeowners can do their own electrical work, but an electrician who is hired must be licensed by the State of Colorado.
LPEA requires the member to have an account number before submitting an interconnection application.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Siting conditions are from the City's undated Solar Permit Checklist.

value.name: Residential solar permit (flat fee)
value.notes: The City's Building Permit Fees page lists this fee for residential solar projects as of 04/01/2026.

value.name: Reinspection fee
value.notes: The City says all failed inspections will be assessed $125.00, paid before the final inspection phase.

permit_fees.notes: As of 04/01/2026, the City's fee for residential solar projects is $125 plus use tax. The City's undated Solar Permit Checklist instead says a $20 solar permit fee must be paid when the permit is issued, so the two City sources give different amounts. Confirm the current fee with the Building Division. On building permits, the City applies use tax at 1.75% of the entire valuation of the project. The State electrical permit and LPEA's $150 Interconnection Application Fee are separate from the City fee.

rebates.notes: LPEA says there are currently no rebates for solar programs.
